EXECUTIVE ORDER 10138
Creating an E mergency B oard T o I nves ­
tigate D ispute  B etween  the T oledo, 
Lorain &  Fairport D ock C ompany  and 
Certain of I ts E mployees
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the Toledo, Lorain &  Fairport Dock Com­
pany, a carrier, and certain of its 
employees represented by the Interna­
tional Longshoremen’ s Association, A. F. 
of L., a labor organization; and 
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provi­
sions of the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as 
to deprive a section of the country of 
essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate the said dispute. No 
member of the said board shall be pe­
cuniarily or otherwise interested in any 
organization of railway employees or 
any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the Toledo, Lorain &  Fairport 
Dock Company or its employees in the 
conditions out of which the said dispute 
arose.

versions.research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10138 (15 FR 4241; govinfo PDF text layer of the official page, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10138 and signed July 3, 1950. The order creates a three-member emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the Toledo, Lorain & Fairport Dock Company and certain of its employees represented by the International Longshoremen's Association, requires the board to report within thirty days from the date of the order. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the board, its thirty-day report deadline and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10138 with a subject line matching this order (creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.

(1) The thirty-day report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21): the order does not end when the board reports, nor when the statutory thirty-day status-quo period after the report runs out; actual report and standstill dates are spent facts that no reviewed event record in this packet supplies, so they are disclosed here rather than recorded as later events. (2) The statutory standstill in section 10 of the Railway Labor Act is the statute's own effect and not a separate command of this order. (3) No later order amends, supersedes or revokes the order before EO 12553 in the held corpus (OFR catalog and number-citation searches). EO 12553 is the first held instrument that revokes it. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order has no command independent of the board's creation and reporting. The thirty-day report requirement and the status-quo sentence are parts of the same board-creating order and share its end; the status-quo sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, whose force comes from that statute.","savings_check":"Savings and residual effects: EO 12553's enacting provision contains no savings or exception clause (the ACT record for this pair lists none, and the held text has none). The board's work, report and any agreement reached are completed past events rather than continuing commands of this order; the order created no right, appointment or transfer that survives independently of it, and no held source shows any continuing independent effect.","scope_check":"Scope: EO 12553 revokes the order by number and the held table row matches its subject; the enacting provision reaches any amendments thereto and has no exception, so it reaches the whole order, not part. The order has no amendment in the held corpus. The dossier lead that each of EO 10138 and EO 10139 is cited by the other arises because both orders are printed on the same Federal Register page (15 FR 4333) and the held text file contains both; neither order's text refers to the other, so no change provision is missing."}

savings_residuals.reason: The revocation has no savings clause and the order created no surviving appointment, transfer or right: bounded search of the held 12553 text, the order's own text and the OFR catalog shows no residual or continuing independent effect.
